subject: PSM
q: Under the National Leprosy Eradication Programme, what is the standard MDT regimen and duration for paucibacillary (PB) leprosy?
why: This is the MB regimen and duration.
Monotherapy is never used because of resistance risk.
Omits Dapsone, a core PB drug.
Correct -- 6 months of monthly Rifampicin plus daily Dapsone.
exp: PB leprosy (2-5 skin lesions, up to 1 nerve involved) is treated with 6 months of monthly supervised Rifampicin plus daily Dapsone; MB leprosy adds Clofazimine and runs 12 months.

subject: PSM
q: Which study design measures disease prevalence rather than incidence, making it best suited to studying chronic conditions of long duration at a single point in time?
why: Cohort studies follow people over time, measuring incidence.
Correct -- captures exposure and outcome at one time point.
Starts with outcome status, estimates odds ratios not prevalence.
Tests interventions, not prevalence.
exp: A cross-sectional study measures exposure and outcome simultaneously in a defined population at one time point, giving a prevalence estimate; it cannot establish temporal sequence or incidence.

subject: PSM
q: The classical epidemiological triad explains disease causation as an interaction between which three factors?
why: Correct -- the foundational causation model.
These are study-design terms, not a causation model.
These are epidemiological measurement terms.
This is the newer social-determinants framing, not the classical triad.
exp: The epidemiological triad (agent-host-environment) is the foundational causation model for infectious and many non-infectious diseases, underlying prevention and vector-control strategy.

subject: PSM
q: Chronic ingestion of methylmercury from contaminated fish, historically linked to industrial effluent discharge into a bay in Japan, causes which environmental disease with neurological damage, ataxia, and congenital neurological defects?
why: Caused by cadmium poisoning affecting bones and kidneys.
Caused by PCB-contaminated rice oil.
Correct -- methylmercury poisoning near Minamata Bay, Japan.
Relates to nitrate-contaminated water causing methemoglobinemia.
exp: Minamata disease resulted from methylmercury-contaminated fish consumption near Minamata Bay (Chisso factory effluent, Japan), causing neurotoxicity and severe congenital neurological damage.

subject: PSM
q: As per UIP schedule guidance, what is the correct route and injection site for Pentavalent vaccine in an infant?
why: Subcutaneous/deltoid is used for MMR, not pentavalent.
Intradermal/forearm is the Mantoux (PPD) test site, not BCG -- BCG itself is intradermal but given over the left deltoid.
Pentavalent is injectable, not oral.
Correct -- IM into anterolateral mid-thigh in infants.
exp: Pentavalent (DPT-HepB-Hib) vaccine is given intramuscularly into the anterolateral aspect of the mid-thigh in infants, where muscle mass is adequate and the sciatic nerve is avoided.

subject: PSM
q: Which anthropometric index best reflects chronic, long-standing undernutrition (stunting), as opposed to acute undernutrition (wasting)?
why: Reflects acute wasting, not chronicity.
Correct -- reflects cumulative long-term nutritional deficit.
Screens for acute severe wasting in the community.
A composite index that cannot distinguish acute from chronic.
exp: Low height-for-age (stunting) reflects cumulative long-term nutritional deficits, while low weight-for-height (wasting) reflects acute recent insult -- the two indices answer different clinical questions.

subject: PSM
q: Under the National Health Mission, which sub-centre level cadre has primary responsibility for vector-control activities and male sterilization (NSV) motivation and follow-up?
why: Correct -- the male counterpart of the ANM, tasked with vector control and NSV follow-up.
Anganwadi worker's mandate is ICDS nutrition/preschool education.
ASHA is a community-level link worker, not sub-centre based.
ANM's core mandate is maternal-child health and family planning for females.
exp: The Multi-Purpose Health Worker (Male) handles vector-borne disease control, TB/leprosy case-holding, and male sterilization promotion/follow-up -- duties outside the ANM's largely MCH-focused role.

subject: PSM
topic: Health Care of The Community in India
q: Under Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY, what is the health cover provided per eligible family per year for secondary and tertiary hospitalisation?
why: Understates the actual cover.
Understates the actual cover.
Correct -- Rs 5 lakh per family per year, cashless.
Overstates the base PM-JAY cover; higher figures apply only in select state top-ups.
exp: PM-JAY provides a cashless health cover of Rs 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalisation, one of the world's largest publicly funded health assurance schemes.

subject: PSM
q: In a cohort study, participants lost to follow-up non-randomly (differently between exposed and unexposed groups) before outcome ascertainment introduce which type of bias?
why: A case-control study problem related to differential memory of past exposure.
Relates to screening/survival-time artifacts.
A third-variable distortion, not a follow-up problem.
Correct -- differential loss to follow-up distorts the true association.
exp: Attrition (loss-to-follow-up) bias occurs when dropout is related to exposure or outcome status, distorting the association; it is a key internal-validity threat in cohort studies, minimised by high follow-up rates.

subject: PSM
q: A 6-year-old child from a sub-Himalayan iodine-deficient belt presents with severe intellectual disability, deaf-mutism, squint, and spasticity, born to a mother with untreated goitre during pregnancy. Which condition best explains this clinical picture?
opts: Endemic (neurological) cretinism due to severe maternal iodine deficiency
Congenital hypothyroidism due to thyroid dysgenesis
why: Correct — endemic cretinism from severe maternal iodine deficiency in an endemic belt
Thyroid dysgenesis is sporadic, not linked to an endemic goitre belt
Vitamin A deficiency causes ocular disease (Bitot spots, xerophthalmia), not this neurological cluster
Kwashiorkor is a protein-energy malnutrition syndrome with edema, unrelated to iodine
exp: Endemic cretinism occurs in severely iodine-deficient regions when maternal hypothyroxinemia during critical fetal brain development causes irreversible neurological damage — intellectual disability, deaf-mutism, squint, spastic diplegia. Unlike sporadic congenital hypothyroidism (thyroid dysgenesis, not geographically clustered), endemic cretinism is preventable by correcting maternal iodine status before and during early pregnancy.

subject: PSM
q: A child screened by an RBSK mobile team for a suspected congenital heart defect is referred onward for confirmation and management. At which facility is this specialist-level confirmation typically coordinated under RBSK?
opts: Village Health and Nutrition Day site
why: Anganwadi is where under-6 children are first screened, not where confirmation happens
Correct — the DEIC houses specialists and coordinates confirmatory diagnosis and management
Sub-centres provide primary-level care, not specialist confirmation
VHNDs are outreach sessions for immunization/ANC, not RBSK referral hubs
exp: Under Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram, children flagged by mobile RBSK teams for the 4D's (Defects at birth, Deficiencies, Diseases, Developmental delays) at community/school level are referred to the District Early Intervention Centre. The DEIC houses specialists who confirm diagnosis, plan management (including free surgery for conditions like congenital heart disease), and arrange follow-up.

subject: PSM
q: During a monsoon-season outbreak in an urban slum, several patients present with sudden-onset profuse painless watery diarrhoea described as 'rice-water' stools, rapidly leading to severe dehydration and hypovolemic shock. Which organism is the most likely cause?
why: Rotavirus is the leading cause of severe childhood diarrhoea generally but not classically an outbreak of rice-water stools
ETEC causes traveller's-diarrhoea-type illness with less severe volume loss
Correct — Vibrio cholerae causes secretory rice-water diarrhoea via cholera toxin
Shigella classically causes dysentery (bloody, mucoid stools with tenesmus), not painless watery stools
exp: Vibrio cholerae produces cholera toxin, which activates adenylate cyclase in enterocytes, causing massive secretory (painless, rice-water) diarrhoea that can produce fatal dehydration within hours. Outbreak management centres on aggressive ORS/IV fluid replacement (Plan C for severe dehydration) and prompt case notification, with antibiotics like doxycycline only as an adjunct.

subject: PSM
topic: Health Care of The Community in India
q: A newly established rural health facility is staffed by one ANM and one male health worker, serving a plain-area population of about 5,000 people, and functions as the first point of contact with the health system. Which facility is this?
why: A PHC serves about 30,000 population and is staffed by a Medical Officer
A CHC serves about 120,000 population with four specialists
District hospitals are secondary/tertiary referral units, not first-contact peripheral facilities
Correct — a Sub-Centre is the most peripheral contact point, serving ~5,000 (plain) population
exp: Under Indian Public Health Standards, a Sub-Centre is the most peripheral point of contact with the health system, staffed by an ANM and typically a Male Health Worker, serving about 5,000 population in plain areas (3,000 in hilly/tribal/difficult areas). It sits one tier below the PHC (30,000 population) in the three-tier rural health pyramid — a numeric fact worth memorising cold for NEET PG.

subject: PSM
q: A public health team, assessing the causes of a community's poor health outcomes, considers four broad determinant categories together: environment, lifestyle/behaviour, biology/heredity, and health care services, weighting environment and lifestyle as the largest contributors. Which conceptual model are they applying?
why: Correct — Blum's four-category model weights environment and lifestyle as the largest contributors
Dahlgren-Whitehead depicts determinants as concentric layers, not Blum's four-category weighting
The epidemiological triad explains infectious disease causation specifically, not general health determinants
Web of causation depicts interlinked contributory causes of a single disease, not a general determinants framework
exp: Blum's model (1974) groups the determinants of health into four categories — environment, lifestyle, heredity/biology, and health care services/system — and assigns environment and lifestyle the greatest relative weight in shaping health status. It is a distinct framework from the Dahlgren-Whitehead 'rainbow' model, which nests social determinants as concentric layers around the individual instead.

subject: PSM
q: A district nodal officer is asked to report progress on a national strategy that targets six beneficiary groups (including children, adolescents, and pregnant women) through six interventions and six institutional mechanisms to reduce anaemia prevalence. Which programme is this?
why: NIPI defines the age-wise IFA dosing schedule itself, not the overarching 6x6x6 strategy
Correct — Anemia Mukt Bharat is the 6 beneficiary groups x 6 interventions x 6 mechanisms strategy
Poshan Abhiyaan is the broader nutrition mission (stunting/wasting/underweight/anaemia), of which AMB is a component
National Deworming Day is a single biannual albendazole intervention, one component within AMB
exp: Anemia Mukt Bharat, launched in 2018 under POSHAN Abhiyaan, uses a life-cycle '6x6x6' strategy: 6 target beneficiary groups (including children 6-59 months, children 5-9 years, adolescents, pregnant and lactating women), 6 interventions (including IFA supplementation, deworming, testing, treatment), and 6 institutional mechanisms. It subsumes and strengthens the older National Iron Plus Initiative's age-wise dosing schedule.

subject: PSM
q: At the state and regional vaccine stores, oral polio vaccine is stored frozen at -15C to -25C, unlike most UIP vaccines which are kept at +2C to +8C throughout the cold chain. What property of OPV explains this exceptional storage requirement?
opts: It is an inactivated vaccine requiring adjuvant stabilisation
It contains aluminium adjuvant which is freeze-labile
It is a live-attenuated vaccine that is highly heat-sensitive, so deep freezing prolongs potency upstream in the chain
It must be reconstituted with a cold-chain-maintained diluent
why: OPV is live-attenuated, not inactivated
Aluminium-adjuvanted vaccines are freeze-sensitive, not OPV, which carries no adjuvant
Correct — OPV is live-attenuated and highly heat-labile, so frozen storage upstream extends its potency
OPV is given as oral drops and does not require reconstitution with a diluent
exp: OPV is a live-attenuated vaccine and among the most heat-labile vaccines used in the UIP. Storing it frozen at state and regional level (before it moves to +2 to +8C at lower tiers for actual field use) maximises its shelf life, whereas freeze-sensitive adsorbed (aluminium-containing) vaccines like DPT and hepatitis B must never be frozen at any tier of the chain — remembering which vaccines tolerate freezing versus which are destroyed by it is a recurring cold-chain theme.

subject: PSM
q: Representatives of all WHO member states convene annually in Geneva to determine WHO policy, approve the programme budget, and oversee the organisation's overall direction. Which body is this?
why: The Executive Board is a smaller elected body that implements WHA decisions, not the supreme policy-setting body
The Secretariat is the administrative staff led by the Director-General, not the policy-setting body
SEARO's Regional Committee governs at the regional, not global, level
Correct — the World Health Assembly is WHO's supreme decision-making body
exp: The World Health Assembly, composed of delegations from all WHO member states, is the organisation's supreme decision-making body. It meets annually in Geneva to set global health policy, approve the programme budget, and oversee WHO's work, while the smaller, elected Executive Board meets more frequently to prepare for and implement the WHA's decisions.

subject: PSM
q: At a Primary Health Centre, the staff member responsible for sanitation surveillance, food and water hygiene inspection, and disease outbreak investigation in the field, distinct from clinical duties, is designated as which functionary?
why: Correct — the Health/Sanitary Inspector handles sanitation surveillance and outbreak field investigation
The ANM/Female Health Worker's role centres on maternal-child health and immunization delivery, not sanitation inspection
The Community Health Officer runs the HWC's clinical/preventive service package, not sanitation surveillance specifically
The Pharmacist dispenses medicines, unrelated to sanitation duties
exp: The Health/Sanitary Inspector is the PHC-level functionary specifically tasked with environmental sanitation, food and water safety surveillance, and epidemiological field investigation of outbreaks — a distinct role from the clinical (Medical Officer) and community nursing (ANM/CHO) cadres that JMOs more often work alongside.

subject: PSM
q: As part of the Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme (IDSP), a rural PHC medical officer reports weekly counts of clinically diagnosed cases of acute diarrhoeal disease to the district surveillance unit, based purely on clinical diagnosis without any laboratory confirmation. Which IDSP reporting form is this?
why: Correct - clinical diagnosis by MO, no lab test, is exactly the P form.
Wrong - L form requires laboratory confirmation.
Wrong - S form is symptom-based reporting by paramedical/community-level workers, not a clinician's diagnosis.
Wrong - media scanning is a separate early-warning component, not a routine reporting form.
exp: IDSP uses a three-tier weekly reporting system - S (syndromic, reported by health workers/ANMs on symptoms), P (presumptive, clinical diagnosis by a medical officer without lab test), and L (laboratory, lab-confirmed) forms - feeding into early outbreak detection at district and state surveillance units.

subject: PSM
q: A study finds that districts with higher per-capita fish consumption have lower cardiovascular mortality rates and concludes that individuals who eat more fish personally have lower cardiovascular risk. This inference is most vulnerable to which error?
why: Correct - this is precisely a group-to-individual inference error.
Wrong - confounding is a distinct issue of a third variable distorting the exposure-outcome link, correctable by adjustment.
Wrong - recall bias applies to differential recall in retrospective studies.
Wrong - lead-time bias relates to apparent survival gain from earlier diagnosis via screening.
exp: Ecological (correlational) studies analyse group/aggregate-level data and can only generate hypotheses; wrongly extrapolating a group-level association to individuals is the ecological fallacy, since the individuals who actually eat more fish within that district may not be the same ones with lower CVD mortality.

subject: PSM
q: A 45-year-old man is found to have radiologically confirmed pulmonary tuberculosis on a routine chest X-ray during a workplace health survey, but he reports no symptoms and continues his normal work. In PSM terminology, he has:
why: Wrong - illness (subjective unwellness) is absent here.
Wrong - sickness requires an assumed social sick role, not applicable to an asymptomatic, functioning worker.
Wrong - contradicts the stem, which states he is asymptomatic and working normally.
Correct - an objective pathological state exists without any subjective feeling of unwellness.
exp: Disease is the objective pathological deviation demonstrable on investigation; illness is the subjective feeling of being unwell; sickness is the social role assumed by, or ascribed to, an unwell person. This asymptomatic screen-detected man has disease without illness, which is exactly why screening programmes exist.

subject: PSM
topic: Health Care of The Community in India
q: Under IPHS norms, a 30-bedded Community Health Centre functioning as a First Referral Unit must be staffed, at minimum, by specialists in which four disciplines?
why: Correct - matches the IPHS-mandated four specialist disciplines at CHC.
Wrong - anaesthetist and orthopaedician are not among the core mandated four.
Wrong - radiologist/pathologist are not part of the core CHC specialist mandate.
Wrong - ENT surgeon is not part of the CHC specialist mandate.
exp: IPHS mandates these four specialists - Surgeon, Physician, OBG, Paediatrician - at CHC level so it can function as a First Referral Unit (FRU) offering comprehensive emergency obstetric and newborn care, backed by support staff and basic OT/blood storage facilities.

subject: PSM
q: A state vaccine store maintains a large walk-in cold storage unit at +2C to +8C for bulk storage of measles and DPT vaccines pending distribution to district stores. This unit is called a:
why: Correct - +2 to +8C bulk storage matches the WIC.
Wrong - a WIF runs at sub-zero temperatures for freezing, not +2 to +8C.
Wrong - deep freezers are smaller units for ice-pack freezing, not bulk vaccine storage at state level.
Wrong - ILRs are used at lower (PHC/CHC) levels, not for state-level bulk storage.
exp: At state and regional vaccine stores, bulk cold-chain storage uses large walk-in units - a Walk-In Cooler (WIC) at +2 to +8C for vaccines like measles and DPT, and a Walk-In Freezer (WIF) at -15 to -25C for OPV bulk storage/ice-pack freezing. ILRs and deep freezers are the smaller units used at lower district/PHC levels.

subject: PSM
q: Under the National Mid-Day Meal Scheme, a child studying in an upper primary school (classes VI-VIII) is entitled to a cooked meal providing a minimum of how many calories and how much protein per school day?
why: Wrong - this is the primary-level (I-V) norm, not upper primary.
Wrong - not the notified figure for either school stage.
Wrong - not the notified figure for either school stage.
Correct - matches the upper-primary MDM calorie/protein norm.
exp: MDM Scheme norms differ by school stage: Primary (classes I-V) = 450 kcal + 12 g protein; Upper Primary (classes VI-VIII) = 700 kcal + 20 g protein per school day - set to supplement dietary intake and improve school attendance and nutritional status.

subject: PSM
q: A below-knee amputee is fitted with a custom-moulded prosthetic limb and later trained in its use and gait pattern. Which allied health professional is primarily responsible for the design, fabrication, and fitting of the prosthetic device itself, as distinct from subsequent gait/functional training?
why: Wrong - physiotherapist handles gait training and mobility rehabilitation after the device is fitted.
Wrong - occupational therapist focuses on adapting activities of daily living.
Correct - P&O professionals design and fit the prosthetic/orthotic device.
Wrong - not a recognised distinct allied health cadre for this function.
exp: Prosthetist and Orthotist (P&O) is a distinct allied health discipline responsible for designing, fabricating, and fitting artificial limbs and orthotic devices; physiotherapists then handle gait and functional training, illustrating the team-based structure of rehabilitation.

subject: PSM
q: As per Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) target 3.2, all countries are to end preventable deaths of newborns and children under 5 years, aiming to reduce the under-5 mortality rate to at least as low as:
why: Wrong - this is the neonatal mortality target, not U5MR.
Correct - matches the SDG 3.2 under-5 mortality target.
Wrong - well above the SDG target ceiling.
Wrong - well above the SDG target ceiling.
exp: SDG target 3.2 actually sets two distinct benchmarks by 2030 - neonatal mortality <=12 per 1000 live births and under-5 mortality <=25 per 1000 live births - and both must be achieved, not just the aggregate U5MR figure.

subject: PSM
q: In a cohort study on smoking and lung cancer, the association between smoking and lung cancer is found to be much stronger in asbestos-exposed workers than in non-exposed workers, with stratified risk estimates differing meaningfully between the two groups. This phenomenon is best described as:
why: Correct - the exposure's effect genuinely differs by strata of a third factor.
Wrong - confounding distorts rather than genuinely modifies the effect, and is handled by adjustment, not description.
Wrong - unrelated to how subjects entered the study.
Wrong - unrelated to the direction of causation.
exp: Effect modification differs fundamentally from confounding: confounding is a bias to be removed by adjustment, whereas effect modification is a genuine biological phenomenon to be reported - here, asbestos and smoking show synergistic (multiplicative) interaction on lung cancer risk.

subject: PSM
q: A population's fasting blood glucose values are approximately normally distributed. Using the statistical (Gaussian) approach to defining normalcy, values are conventionally considered normal if they lie within:
why: Wrong - covers only about 68% of the population, too narrow, misclassifying many healthy people as abnormal.
Wrong - too wide, would miss genuinely abnormal values.
Correct - the conventional mean +/- 2 SD cutoff.
Wrong - that is a non-Gaussian, distribution-free approach.
exp: The statistical/Gaussian approach to defining normalcy sets normal as mean +/- 2 SD, encompassing about 95% of a normally distributed population - a purely statistical convention that need not equal true clinical or biological normalcy.

subject: PSM
q: Under the Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK), what is guaranteed to every pregnant woman delivering in a public health institution in India?
opts: A cash incentive only, with no free services provided
Free antenatal care only, while delivery charges still apply
Free drugs, diagnostics, diet, blood, and free transport (both ways, extended to sick infants up to 1 year), with zero out-of-pocket expenditure
Free services, but only for BPL cardholders
why: JSSK is a service-entitlement scheme, not a cash-transfer scheme; Janani Suraksha Yojana is the cash-incentive scheme
Both antenatal and delivery services are covered free under JSSK, not just antenatal care
Correct: JSSK is a comprehensive, universal, zero out-of-pocket entitlement for institutional delivery and related care
JSSK applies universally to all women delivering in public institutions, not restricted to BPL status
exp: JSSK, launched in 2011, guarantees zero out-of-pocket expenditure for institutional delivery (including cesarean section), covering free drugs and consumables, diagnostics, diet, blood transfusion, and free transport to and from the facility, extended to sick neonates up to one year of age.

subject: PSM
q: A neonate born to an HIV-positive mother is confirmed to have symptomatic HIV infection at birth. What is done regarding BCG vaccination?
opts: BCG is given at birth as per the routine UIP schedule regardless of HIV status
BCG is replaced with IPV in all HIV-exposed infants
A double dose of BCG is given for added protection

BCG is withheld in any child confirmed HIV-infected, symptomatic or not, unless on ART, clinically well, and immunologically stable, being a live vaccine; it is still given per schedule if the infant is HIV-exposed but of unknown or negative status
why: This ignores the live-vaccine contraindication in confirmed infection
IPV is an inactivated polio vaccine and is unrelated to, and not a substitute for, BCG
Vaccine dose is never doubled for any indication
Correct: as a live attenuated vaccine, BCG risks disseminated BCG disease in an immunocompromised host and is withheld in confirmed HIV infection regardless of symptoms, per current WHO guidance
exp: BCG is a live attenuated vaccine carrying a risk of disseminated BCG disease (BCGosis) in an immunocompromised host. Current WHO guidance (2018 revision) withholds BCG in any child with confirmed HIV infection, symptomatic or not, unless the child is on ART, clinically well, and immunologically stable; HIV-exposed infants of unknown or negative status still get BCG at birth per the routine UIP schedule.

subject: PSM
q: As per the National Iodine Deficiency Disorders Control Programme (NIDDCP), what is the minimum recommended iodine content of salt at the consumer/household level?
why: Correct: NIDDCP specifies a minimum of 15 ppm iodine content at the consumer/household level
5 ppm is below the effective protective threshold specified by the programme
30 ppm is the production-level specification, accounting for storage/transport losses, not the consumer-level minimum
50 ppm exceeds the recommended level and risks iodine-induced thyroid dysfunction
exp: NIDDCP mandates a minimum iodine content of 15 ppm at the consumer/household level, with a higher figure specified at the point of production to allow for losses during transport and storage, to protect against iodine deficiency disorders such as goitre and cretinism.

subject: PSM
q: As per India Meteorological Department (IMD) criteria used in Heat Action Plans, what defines a heat wave over the plains?
opts: Maximum temperature 35 degrees C or higher regardless of departure from normal
Maximum temperature 40 degrees C or higher with a departure of 4.5 degrees C or more from normal, OR an actual maximum temperature of 45 degrees C or higher irrespective of departure from normal
Minimum temperature 30 degrees C or higher for 3 consecutive days
Any temperature above 37 degrees C for 2 consecutive days
why: This omits the departure-from-normal criterion that is central to the IMD definition
Correct: IMD defines a heat wave using a maximum temperature threshold combined with departure from normal, or an absolute high-temperature threshold regardless of departure
This uses minimum temperature, which is not the IMD heat wave parameter
This is an arbitrary threshold not used in the national criteria
exp: IMD defines a heat wave over the plains as a maximum temperature of at least 40 degrees C with a departure from normal of roughly 4-6 degrees C depending on the station's own normal (severe heat wave at roughly 6-7 degrees C departure), or an absolute maximum of 45 degrees C or higher regardless of departure (severe at 47 degrees C or higher), a threshold that triggers Heat Action Plan alerts. Exact departure bands vary slightly between IMD and NDMA sources, so treat the numbers as indicative rather than fixed.

subject: PSM
q: A patient with cough for 3 weeks is smear-negative but Xpert MTB/RIF positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis, rifampicin-sensitive. Under India's National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP), this patient is classified as:
why: Presumptive TB describes a person with TB-suggestive symptoms before testing; this patient has already tested positive
Clinically diagnosed TB applies only in the absence of bacteriological confirmation, which is not the case here
Correct: detection of M. tuberculosis by a WHO-approved rapid molecular test, culture, or smear classifies the case as bacteriologically confirmed, regardless of smear result
This patient is rifampicin-sensitive, so drug-resistant TB does not apply
exp: Under NTEP, any patient in whom M. tuberculosis is detected by a WHO-approved rapid molecular test such as Xpert MTB/RIF, by culture, or by smear microscopy is classified as bacteriologically confirmed TB, distinct from clinically diagnosed TB which relies on clinical or radiological grounds alone.

subject: PSM
q: A new screening test is applied in a population with very low disease prevalence. Sensitivity and specificity of the test remain unchanged. What happens to its negative predictive value (NPV)?
opts: NPV becomes numerically equal to specificity
why: This describes what happens to positive predictive value, not negative predictive value, as prevalence falls
Predictive values are prevalence-dependent, unlike sensitivity and specificity, which are intrinsic properties of the test
NPV equals specificity only in a specific mathematical special case, not as a general rule
Correct: as prevalence falls, a negative result is even more likely to be a true negative, so NPV rises toward 100 percent
exp: Predictive values are prevalence-dependent, unlike sensitivity and specificity which are fixed test properties: as disease prevalence falls, negative predictive value rises toward 100 percent while positive predictive value falls - a frequently tested epidemiology concept.

subject: PSM
q: A child already suffering from acute diarrhoea is given oral rehydration therapy to prevent dehydration and death. This intervention is an example of which level of prevention?
why: Correct: this is early treatment of already-established disease to prevent its immediate complications, the definition of secondary prevention
Primordial prevention targets underlying determinants before risk factors even arise, such as promoting safe water supply
Primary prevention acts before disease onset, such as hand-hygiene education to prevent diarrhoea from occurring at all
Tertiary prevention addresses established long-term sequelae, such as managing chronic malnutrition after repeated diarrhoeal illness
exp: Secondary prevention means early detection and treatment of disease that has already occurred, to halt its progression and prevent immediate complications - giving ORT to a child already having diarrhoea to prevent dehydration and death is a textbook example.

subject: PSM
topic: Health Care of The Community in India
q: In India's three-tier rural health care system, which sequence correctly represents the referral pyramid from the periphery to the center?
opts: CHC then PHC then Sub-centre then District Hospital
Sub-centre then PHC then CHC then District Hospital
PHC then Sub-centre then CHC then District Hospital
Sub-centre then CHC then PHC then District Hospital
why: This reverses the correct order, incorrectly starting from the Community Health Centre
Correct: the pyramid ascends from Sub-centre (most peripheral) through PHC and CHC to the District Hospital (apex)
This incorrectly places the PHC below the Sub-centre in the sequence
This incorrectly places the CHC before the PHC in the sequence
exp: India's rural health referral pyramid ascends as Sub-centre (first contact, staffed by an ANM/health worker) to Primary Health Centre (first medical officer contact) to Community Health Centre (designated first referral unit with specialist care) to District Hospital (apex referral institution).

subject: PSM
q: The Vaccine Vial Monitor (VVM) is affixed directly to the vaccine vial or ampoule itself, not just the outer carton, because it is designed to:
opts: Indicate the vaccine's printed expiry date
Detect freezing damage in freeze-sensitive vaccines
Record the cumulative heat exposure of that specific vial, giving a real-time indicator of whether the vaccine inside remains potent
Confirm the cold chain was maintained only during manufacturing, not during field use
why: Expiry date is a separate printed label and is unrelated to the VVM's function
Freezing damage is assessed by the shake test or a freeze-tag/freeze indicator, since the VVM responds to heat exposure, not cold
Correct: the VVM changes color irreversibly in proportion to cumulative heat exposure, giving a real-time potency check at the point of use
The VVM's entire value is that it functions throughout the supply chain including the point of vaccination in the field, not only during manufacture
exp: A Vaccine Vial Monitor is a heat-sensitive label placed on the individual vial that changes color irreversibly with cumulative time-temperature exposure, allowing a real-time check at every level of the cold chain, including the moment of vaccination, of whether that specific vial remains potent.

subject: PSM
q: Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Food (RUTF), used for community-based outpatient management of uncomplicated severe acute malnutrition (SAM), is typically based on which combination of ingredients?
opts: Skimmed milk powder with a cereal-based porridge
Soy protein isolate with added iron only
Plain full-cream milk with added glucose
Peanut/groundnut paste fortified with milk powder, sugar, vegetable oil, and added vitamins and minerals
why: Skimmed milk-cereal porridge formulations such as F-75/F-100 are used for inpatient, facility-based management of complicated SAM, not the take-home RUTF
This is not the standard RUTF composition
This lacks the energy density and micronutrient fortification that RUTF requires
Correct: RUTF is a lipid-based, energy-dense, micronutrient-fortified peanut paste formulation
exp: RUTF is a lipid-based paste of roughly 500 kcal per 100 g, classically made from peanut/groundnut paste, milk powder, sugar, and vegetable oil with added micronutrients, requiring no water or cooking, which is what enables safe outpatient community-based management of uncomplicated SAM.

subject: PSM
q: Which community-based screening tool for diabetes risk in India assigns points for age, waist circumference, family history of diabetes, and level of physical activity?
why: Correct
A similar Finnish tool with different parameters
A broader NCD surveillance survey, not this specific score
Predicts cardiovascular risk, not diabetes risk
exp: The Indian Diabetes Risk Score (IDRS), developed by the Madras Diabetes Research Foundation, is a validated 4-parameter opportunistic community screening tool (age, waist circumference, family history, physical activity) for population-level diabetes risk screening in India.

subject: PSM
q: Which statistical measure assesses the level of agreement between two observers rating the same set of subjects, beyond what would be expected by chance alone?
why: Measures linear relationship strength, not rater agreement
Tests categorical association, not agreement corrected for chance
Correct
Compares incidence in exposed vs unexposed, unrelated to rater agreement
exp: The kappa statistic measures inter-observer agreement corrected for the agreement expected by chance alone; a kappa near 1 indicates near-perfect agreement, while a value near 0 indicates agreement no better than chance.

subject: PSM
q: As per the WHO (1948) definition, health is a state of complete physical, mental, and _____ well-being, and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity.
why: Not part of the original 1948 definition
Correct
Not the specific WHO term used
Not part of the definition
exp: The WHO's 1948 constitution defines health as 'a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being, and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity' — a positive, holistic definition still foundational to PSM.

subject: PSM
q: As per CPCB Noise Pollution Rules, the permissible ambient noise level in a residential area during daytime is:
why: Correct, residential daytime limit
This is the residential night limit, not day
This is the commercial zone day limit
This is the industrial zone day limit
exp: Under India's Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000, ambient noise limits are: Residential 55 dB(A) day / 45 dB(A) night; Commercial 65/55; Industrial 75/70; Silence zone 50/40 — a frequently tested PSM number.

subject: PSM
q: Which cold chain equipment is used to carry vaccines from the PHC/CHC to an outreach session site, keeping them at +2C to +8C for several hours using conditioned ice packs?
why: Used for bulk/longer-distance transport, not routine session carriage
Correct — the small field-transport container
Generates ice packs, does not carry vaccines
Fixed storage equipment at the health facility, not for field carriage
exp: ⚠️ The vaccine carrier is the small, ice-pack-lined container used to carry vaccines from the health facility to the session site (commonly cited as maintaining cold chain for around 12 hours with 4 ice packs — verify the exact figure in the current GOI handbook); the cold box is used for bulkier/longer transport, and the ILR/deep freezer are fixed cold-chain storage points.

subject: PSM
q: As per IAP recommendations, all exclusively breastfed infants should receive a daily oral Vitamin D supplementation dose of:
why: Sub-therapeutic, insufficient dose
Closer to a treatment dose for diagnosed deficiency, not routine prophylaxis
Correct prophylactic dose
Exceeds the recommended prophylactic dose
exp: IAP (aligned with AAP) recommends 400 IU/day of Vitamin D from birth for exclusively and partially breastfed infants regardless of sun exposure, continued until adequate dietary/sunlight-derived intake is established — a simple, frequently tested dose.

subject: PSM
q: The primary treatment goal of an occupational therapist in a rehabilitation team is to help the patient:
opts: Correct musculoskeletal deformities using passive stretching and electrotherapy
Diagnose and treat speech and swallowing disorders
Fabricate and fit custom prosthetic limbs
Regain functional independence in activities of daily living using adaptive techniques and assistive devices
why: Describes physiotherapy's domain
Describes the speech-language pathologist's role
Describes the prosthetist-orthotist's role
Correct
exp: Occupational therapy restores a person's ability to perform activities of daily living (dressing, feeding, bathing, work tasks) via adaptive strategies and assistive devices — distinct from physiotherapy (musculoskeletal function), speech-language pathology, and prosthetics/orthotics.

subject: PSM
topic: Health Care of The Community in India
q: As per Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS), a Primary Health Centre (PHC) in a plain area is designed to serve a population of:
why: This is the sub-centre norm
Correct
This is the CHC norm for hilly/tribal areas
This is the CHC norm for plain areas
exp: IPHS population norms (plain area): Sub-centre 5,000, PHC 30,000, CHC 1,20,000 (halved roughly for hilly/tribal/difficult areas) — the backbone numbers for India's public health pyramid.

subject: PSM
q: In a study of coffee intake and lung cancer, cigarette smoking is associated with both the exposure and the outcome but does not lie on the causal pathway between them. Smoking here acts as a:
why: Correct
An effect modifier changes the strength/direction of an association, it is not merely associated with both variables
A mediator lies on the causal pathway, which smoking here does not
Selection bias arises from how subjects are chosen into the study, not from a third variable
exp: A confounder is an extraneous factor associated with both exposure and outcome, not on the causal pathway, that distorts the true association unless controlled for by stratification, matching, or multivariate adjustment.

subject: PSM
q: Health planners evaluating a chronic disease for a national screening programme note it has a recognizable latent asymptomatic phase, an accepted effective treatment exists once detected, and a suitable, acceptable diagnostic test is available. These conditions together best satisfy which framework?
why: Bradford Hill criteria are used to judge causal association between an exposure and outcome, not screening programme suitability.
There is no standard Wilson's criteria for outbreak investigation - a distractor conflating names.
Correct - Wilson and Jungner screening criteria.
WHO case definitions standardize diagnosis for surveillance purposes, unrelated to screening programme design.
exp: The Wilson and Jungner criteria (WHO, 1968) are the classic ten principles for deciding whether a disease is suitable for population screening - covering disease importance, a recognizable latent stage, an accepted treatment, a suitable test, and cost-effectiveness of the programme - the reference framework for any screening policy discussion.

subject: PSM
q: An ASHA worker facilitates institutional delivery for a pregnant woman from a rural area in a Low Performing State under a scheme that provides direct cash assistance to promote institutional delivery. Which national scheme is this?
why: Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK) entitles pregnant women and sick neonates to free delivery, drugs, diagnostics, diet and transport - a service-guarantee scheme, not primarily a cash-incentive scheme.
PMSMA provides free comprehensive antenatal care on the 9th of every month, not a delivery cash incentive.
LaQshya is a quality-improvement initiative for labour rooms and maternity operation theatres, not a cash transfer scheme.
Correct - Janani Suraksha Yojana.
exp: Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY), launched in 2005 under the National Health Mission, is a conditional cash transfer scheme paying differential incentives to mother and ASHA based on rural/urban and LPS/HPS status, to promote institutional delivery. Exact cash amounts by category should be verified against the current NHM guideline.

subject: PSM
q: At a Primary Health Centre, OPV and measles vaccine are stored in the same cold chain equipment as all other UIP vaccines. What temperature range is this equipment maintained at?
why: Wrong at PHC level - deep freezer is used only for ice-pack prep at PHC, and for bulk storage at district level and above
Correct - the ILR stores all UIP vaccines including OPV and measles at PHC level
Not a standard UIP cold chain storage range
Colder than any standard UIP cold chain equipment setting
exp: At Primary Health Centre level, all UIP vaccines - including OPV and measles - are stored together in the Ice-Lined Refrigerator (ILR) at +2C to +8C; the PHC's deep freezer is used only for freezing ice packs, not vaccine storage. Bulk deep-freezer storage of OPV/measles at -15C to -25C happens only at district level and above, before distribution to PHCs.

subject: PSM
q: A low-income country receives financial and technical support to introduce pneumococcal conjugate vaccine into its national immunization programme, from a public-private global health partnership headquartered in Geneva. Which organization provides this support?
opts: Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria
why: The Global Fund finances programmes against HIV, TB and malaria specifically, not vaccine introduction.
Correct - Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance.
UNICEF procures and distributes vaccines and supports immunization logistics but is not itself the financing partnership described.
WHO SEARO is a WHO regional office (New Delhi) providing technical guidance, not the vaccine-financing alliance described.
exp: Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, is a public-private global health partnership headquartered in Geneva that funds and supports the introduction of new and underused vaccines into low-income countries' national immunization programmes, distinct from the Global Fund's HIV/TB/malaria focus.

subject: PSM
q: A functionary based at the Anganwadi Centre under the ICDS scheme is primarily responsible for supplementary nutrition, pre-school non-formal education, and growth monitoring of children under six years. Who is this functionary?
why: ASHA is a community health activist under NHM, focused on linking the community to health services, not the ICDS pre-school/nutrition functionary.
ANM (Auxiliary Nurse Midwife) is a clinical/nursing functionary at the sub-centre, not based at the Anganwadi Centre.
Correct - Anganwadi Worker.
Community Health Officer (CHO) staffs the Health and Wellness Centre under Ayushman Bharat, a different, more recent cadre.
exp: The Anganwadi Worker (AWW), a community-based honorary worker under ICDS, delivers the six ICDS services at the Anganwadi Centre - supplementary nutrition, referral, pre-school non-formal education, nutrition/health education, and growth monitoring - distinct from ASHA and ANM.

subject: PSM
q: Under the National Filariasis Elimination Programme, annual Mass Drug Administration in high-endemic districts increasingly uses a triple-drug regimen instead of the earlier two-drug regimen. Which combination is this?
why: DEC + Albendazole alone is the older two-drug MDA regimen still used in many districts, but not the newer triple-drug combination asked here.
Ivermectin + Doxycycline is not a standard MDA combination for lymphatic filariasis in India.
Albendazole + Praziquantel is not a filariasis regimen; praziquantel is used for schistosomiasis/cestode infections.
Correct - DEC + Albendazole + Ivermectin (IDA) triple-drug therapy.
exp: Since 2018, India has progressively rolled out triple-drug therapy - DEC + Albendazole + Ivermectin (IDA) - for annual MDA in selected high-microfilaria-rate districts, replacing the earlier DEC+Albendazole regimen, to accelerate interruption of lymphatic filariasis transmission. District-level rollout specifics should be verified against the current NVBDCP guideline.

subject: PSM
q: A factory's workforce shows a higher observed number of deaths from a specific cancer than expected based on age-adjusted national mortality rates. Which measure compares observed to expected deaths in this occupational cohort?
why: Correct - Standardized Mortality Ratio.
Case Fatality Rate measures the proportion of diagnosed cases that die from a specific disease, not a comparison to an expected count in a cohort.
Proportional Mortality Ratio compares the proportion of deaths from a specific cause within the study group to a reference group, a related but distinct measure.
Crude Death Rate is simply total deaths per population per year, with no adjustment for age structure or comparison to expected counts.
exp: The Standardized Mortality Ratio (SMR) compares observed deaths in a study population to the number expected if it had experienced a reference population's age- and sex-specific mortality rates, expressed as (Observed/Expected) x 100 - a mainstay of occupational epidemiology.

subject: PSM
q: During municipal water treatment, chlorine is added until the point beyond which further addition causes a proportional rise in free residual chlorine, after destroying ammonia and organic matter. This point is called?
why: Superchlorination refers to deliberately adding chlorine well in excess of normal requirements, a related but distinct concept from the break-point itself.
Correct - break-point chlorination.
Dechlorination is the deliberate removal of excess chlorine after superchlorination, the opposite process.
Dosing point is not a standard technical term in this context.
exp: Break-point chlorination is the point on the chlorine dose-residual curve at which all chlorine-demand-exerting substances have been oxidized, so any further chlorine added appears as free available residual chlorine - dosing just beyond this point ensures adequate disinfection with a measurable free residual.

subject: PSM
q: A pregnant woman tests positive for HIV during antenatal screening at a Primary Health Centre and is started on lifelong antiretroviral therapy irrespective of her CD4 count, with the infant given prophylaxis after birth. This falls under which national programme component?
opts: Prevention of Parent to Child Transmission (PPTCT) under NACP
why: RBSK is a child screening and early intervention programme for defects, deficiencies, diseases and developmental delays, unrelated to HIV in pregnancy.
PMSMA provides free comprehensive antenatal check-ups on a fixed day each month, not specifically the HIV ART pathway.
Correct - PPTCT under NACP.
Mission Indradhanush is an intensified routine immunization drive for unvaccinated/partially vaccinated children, unrelated to HIV prevention in pregnancy.
exp: Prevention of Parent to Child Transmission (PPTCT), under the National AIDS Control Programme, follows the WHO Option B+ strategy - lifelong ART in every HIV-positive pregnant or breastfeeding woman regardless of CD4 count, plus infant prophylaxis and early infant diagnosis, to virtually eliminate mother-to-child HIV transmission.

subject: PSM
q: As per Universal Immunization Programme guidelines, which type of syringe is mandatorily used at all UIP sessions to prevent reuse and ensure injection safety?
why: Glass syringes were used historically but are not the current UIP standard, since they require sterilization between uses and risk cross-contamination.
Insulin syringes are calibrated for insulin dosing (units), not standard immunization use.
Tuberculin syringes are used for intradermal tests and BCG, but are not the general mandated UIP injection safety device for all vaccines.
Correct - Auto-Disable (AD) syringes are mandatory across the UIP.
exp: Auto-Disable (AD) syringes, which lock and become unusable after a single use, have been mandatory for all UIP immunization sessions in India since the mid-2000s, specifically to eliminate the risk of syringe reuse and blood-borne infection transmission during mass immunization drives.

subject: PSM
q: Under the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) scheme, which frontline worker is primarily responsible for delivering supplementary nutrition, pre-school non-formal education, and growth monitoring at the anganwadi centre?
why: Wrong — ASHA is an NHM community link worker, not part of ICDS delivery.
Wrong — ANM provides clinical MCH services at the sub-centre level.
Correct — the Anganwadi Worker is the ICDS frontline functionary delivering the six ICDS services from the anganwadi centre.
Wrong — MPHW handles broader public-health and disease-control duties.
exp: Distinguish the three key frontline village-level workers: ASHA (NHM, community mobilization), ANM (sub-centre, clinical MCH services), and Anganwadi Worker (ICDS, nutrition and pre-school education) — a favorite 'who does what' PSM question.

subject: PSM
q: Histopathological examination of brain tissue from a person who died of suspected rabies shows characteristic eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusion bodies in Purkinje cells and pyramidal neurons. What are these inclusions called?
why: Wrong — seen in yellow fever (apoptotic hepatocytes).
Wrong — seen in smallpox/vaccinia infection.
Wrong — the pathognomonic granuloma of rheumatic fever.
Correct — pathognomonic post-mortem finding confirming rabies.
exp: Negri bodies remain the classic post-mortem histopathological confirmation of rabies, though direct fluorescent antibody testing on brain tissue is now the gold standard. Rabies is 100% fatal once symptomatic, making pre/post-exposure prophylaxis the entire management strategy.

subject: PSM
q: In a stable population, prevalence is related to incidence and average duration of disease by which formula?
opts: Prevalence = Incidence x Mean duration of disease
Prevalence = Incidence divided by Mean duration of disease
Incidence = Prevalence x Mean duration of disease
Prevalence and incidence are unrelated for chronic diseases
why: Correct — for diseases with low, fairly constant prevalence, P is approximately I x D.
Wrong — inverts the relationship.
Wrong — transposes the formula incorrectly.
Wrong — the two are mathematically related, not independent.
exp: The relationship P = I x D explains why a disease with high incidence but short duration (common cold) can have low prevalence, while a disease with low incidence but long duration (diabetes, HIV on treatment) accumulates high prevalence.

subject: PSM
q: As per the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDG 3), what is the global target for maternal mortality ratio (MMR) to be achieved by 2030?
why: Wrong — closer to an older MDG-era benchmark.
Correct — SDG 3.1 sets a global target of MMR below 70 per 100,000 live births by 2030.
Wrong — lower than the stated global SDG target.
Wrong — lower than the stated global SDG target.
exp: Flag: SDG 3.1 global MMR target (under 70 per 100,000 live births by 2030) should be verified against the latest WHO/NHM document, as India's own national MMR target under national programmes may differ from the global SDG figure and both get asked.

subject: PSM
q: A newborn in a district hospital fails the automated otoacoustic emissions (OAE) hearing screening test performed before discharge. Under which national programme is this universal newborn hearing screening mandated, with further referral for diagnostic ABR testing and early intervention if confirmed?
opts: National Programme for Prevention and Control of Deafness (NPPCD)
why: Correct — RBSK's delivery-point OAE screening plus DEIC referral for diagnostic ABR and early intervention matches this pathway.
Wrong — Mission Indradhanush is an immunization catch-up drive.
Wrong — NPPCD is primarily an ENT-services and hearing-aid-distribution programme; universal newborn screening is not its established core mandate.
Wrong — PMSMA is an antenatal care programme.
exp: RBSK's 4-D's screening ('Defects at birth') includes congenital deafness — OAE is done at the delivery point by the Medical Officer/Staff Nurse/ANM before discharge (and again by the ANM during home visits up to 6 weeks under HBNC); screen-positive infants are referred to the District Early Intervention Centre (DEIC) for diagnostic ABR/BERA, and confirmed cases receive free early intervention (hearing aid/cochlear implant, speech therapy).

subject: PSM
q: A health worker at a sub-centre immunization session reconstitutes BCG vaccine using a diluent that was left out at room temperature overnight instead of being stored with the vaccine vials. What is the most likely consequence for the vaccinated infants?
opts: Reduced vaccine potency, since diluents for freeze-dried vaccines must be kept in the cold chain (2-8°C) before use
No effect, since diluents are inert and do not affect potency
Increased risk of anaphylaxis from the warmed diluent
Vaccine failure only if the diluent had been frozen, not if kept warm
why: Correct — diluent must be pre-cooled with the vaccine; a warm diluent degrades reconstituted live-vaccine potency.
Wrong — diluent temperature directly affects viability of the reconstituted live vaccine; it is not inert to this process.
Wrong — a warm diluent causes reduced potency, not an allergic/anaphylactic reaction.
Wrong — both freezing and warming the diluent are cold-chain errors; the freezing-only claim is incomplete.
exp: Diluents supplied with freeze-dried vaccines (BCG, measles/MR) must be stored in the cold chain at 2-8°C alongside the vaccine and never left at room temperature or frozen. Reconstituting with a warm diluent accelerates degradation of the live attenuated vaccine and reduces potency, even though the diluent itself looks unchanged — a commonly missed cold-chain error distinct from mishandling the vaccine vial itself.

subject: PSM
q: A 14-month-old child with severe acute malnutrition (weight-for-height less than -3 SD, no bilateral pitting edema, no medical complications, and passing the appetite test) is being managed in the community. What is the recommended approach?
opts: Immediate hospitalization and F-75 therapeutic milk
Hospitalization with F-100 therapeutic milk until full recovery
IV fluids and broad-spectrum antibiotics as inpatient
Community-based management with Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Food (RUTF) on an outpatient basis
why: Wrong — F-75 is the inpatient stabilization feed for complicated SAM, not needed here.
Wrong — F-100 is used for inpatient rehabilitation, not indicated for uncomplicated SAM.
Wrong — reserved for complicated SAM with danger signs.
Correct — uncomplicated SAM is managed in the community with RUTF under India's community-based management approach.
exp: SAM triage hinges on the appetite test and presence of complications or edema: complicated SAM needs inpatient care with F-75 then F-100/RUTF per WHO protocol; uncomplicated SAM goes to outpatient community management with RUTF and weekly follow-up, avoiding unnecessary hospitalization.

subject: PSM
q: A hospital's biomedical waste management team is segregating waste at the point of generation. Used IV cannulas, needles, and other sharps are placed into which color-coded bag/container as per Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules?
why: Correct — sharps go into white translucent, puncture-proof, leak-proof containers.
Wrong — yellow is for anatomical/soiled waste and expired medicines.
Wrong — red is for recyclable items like tubing and catheters.
Wrong — blue is for glassware/metallic implants, a separate category.
exp: Flag: colour-coding under Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules 2016 (as amended) has been revised more than once — verify the current category against the latest CPCB guideline; broadly yellow is incinerable waste, red is recyclable, white/translucent is sharps, blue is glassware/metallic implants.

subject: PSM
q: A 6-year-old from a rice-paddy and pig-rearing area of eastern Uttar Pradesh presents in the monsoon with high fever, altered sensorium, and seizures; CSF shows lymphocytic pleocytosis with normal sugar. Which vector-borne disease fits best, and what is its amplifying host?
opts: Dengue encephalopathy, with humans as the amplifying host
Nipah virus encephalitis, with fruit bats as the reservoir
Japanese encephalitis, with pigs as the amplifying host
Scrub typhus, with chigger mites as the vector
why: Dengue causes an encephalopathy from cerebral edema/metabolic derangement, not classic viral encephalitis with an animal amplifier
Nipah is linked to fruit bats and pig farms in specific outbreak settings, not this typical paddy-pig ecology
This correctly matches JE's classic epidemiological triad
Scrub typhus presents with an eschar and is transmitted by trombiculid mite larvae, not through this pig-paddy ecology
exp: Japanese encephalitis is transmitted by Culex mosquitoes with pigs as the key amplifying host and ardeid birds as reservoirs - the pig-rearing, paddy-field ecology plus monsoon timing and CSF picture are the classic exam triad; India vaccinates against JE in endemic districts under the national immunization schedule.

subject: PSM
q: In a population, the incidence of a disease among smokers is 40 per 1000 and among non-smokers is 10 per 1000; the overall population incidence is 25 per 1000. What is the population attributable risk percentage (PAR%)?
why: This would result from a different, incorrect denominator/numerator pairing
This is the correct PAR% calculation
This equals the attributable risk percent among the exposed, (Ie-Iu)/Ie x100 = 75%, a common confusion with PAR%
This is simply the raw incidence value among smokers (40 per 1000) misread as a percentage, not a computed measure
exp: PAR% = (Incidence in total population - Incidence in unexposed) / Incidence in total population x 100 = (25-10)/25 x 100 = 60% - this tells policymakers what fraction of total disease burden in the whole population would be eliminated if smoking were removed, factoring in prevalence of exposure.

subject: PSM
q: A PHC team actively screens the community, identifies a sputum-positive TB patient through active case finding, and starts DOTS therapy immediately to interrupt transmission. Which level of prevention does this represent?
why: This correctly identifies early diagnosis and treatment as secondary prevention
Primary prevention would be BCG vaccination or health education before disease onset
Primordial prevention targets underlying social/economic determinants before risk factors even emerge
Tertiary prevention is rehabilitation/disability limitation after disease has caused damage
exp: Secondary prevention aims at early diagnosis and prompt treatment to halt disease progression and interrupt transmission at the community level - active case finding plus immediate DOTS initiation is the textbook example.

subject: PSM
q: A country detects a novel respiratory pathogen with sustained human-to-human transmission and must notify WHO within 24 hours of assessing it as a potential public health emergency of international concern. Which international instrument creates this legal obligation?
why: Alma-Ata (1978) established Primary Health Care and Health for All goals, not outbreak notification law
FCTC is WHO's tobacco-control treaty, unrelated to outbreak reporting
SDGs are development goals/targets, not a notification framework
IHR 2005 is correctly the binding instrument for international disease reporting
exp: The IHR (2005), a legally binding WHO instrument for all member states, obliges countries to notify WHO of events that may constitute a Public Health Emergency of International Concern and mandates core surveillance/response capacities at points of entry.

subject: PSM
q: A field worker packs a vaccine carrier with icepacks taken straight from the deep freezer (about -20C) to transport DPT and TT vials to an outreach immunization session. What is the error here, and what is its consequence?
opts: Icepacks should always be used frozen directly for every vaccine
Conditioning of icepacks is required only during summer months
Icepacks must first be conditioned (partially thawed until sweating/free water appears) before packing freeze-sensitive vaccines
Only cold boxes need conditioned icepacks, not vaccine carriers
why: Using frozen icepacks directly against freeze-sensitive vaccines destroys their potency
Conditioning is required year-round whenever freeze-sensitive vaccines are transported, not just in summer
This correctly explains that conditioning prevents freeze damage to DPT/TT/HepB
Both cold boxes and vaccine carriers require conditioned icepacks when carrying freeze-sensitive vaccines
exp: DPT, TT, Td, Hepatitis B, and pentavalent vaccines are freeze-sensitive (unlike OPV and measles, which are freeze-tolerant but heat-labile), so icepacks used alongside them must be conditioned by leaving them at room temperature until they reach 0C and show visible surface water. Flag: verify exact wording against the current Government of India Cold Chain and Vaccine Management handbook.

subject: PSM
q: A 3-year-old presents with dry, foamy, triangular grey patches on the bulbar conjunctiva along with a history of night blindness. Which WHO clinical stage of xerophthalmia does this represent?
opts: X3A - corneal ulceration/keratomalacia (less than 1/3 of cornea)
why: Night blindness alone (XN) is a functional stage without a visible conjunctival lesion
This correctly identifies the described lesion as X1B, Bitot's spots
X2 involves the cornea (dry, hazy, non-ulcerated), not conjunctival patches
X3A denotes active corneal ulceration, a more severe stage than described here
exp: Bitot's spots (foamy, triangular, grey conjunctival patches, classically at the temporal limbus, caused by keratinizing squamous metaplasia and gas-forming Corynebacterium xerosis) define WHO stage X1B and warrant treatment-dose vitamin A, not just prophylactic dosing.

subject: PSM
q: At a school health screening camp, a trained non-physician professional performs visual acuity testing and prescribes corrective spectacles, but refers cases with red eye or suspected cataract onward for medical/surgical management. Which allied health cadre performed this screening role?
why: Optometrists are a separate, largely private-sector cadre and are not the personnel deployed under the NPCB in government school-screening camps
An ophthalmologist is a physician who manages disease and performs surgery, not the primary school-screening cadre
Orthoptists specialize in binocular vision/squint assessment, not general school vision screening
This is precisely the NPCB Ophthalmic Assistant's defined role
exp: Under India's National Programme for Control of Blindness (NPCB/NPCBVI), school eye-screening camps are staffed by trained Paramedical Ophthalmic Assistants - they test visual acuity, perform refraction, and dispense corrective spectacles at the PHC/vision-centre level, referring red eye, suspected cataract, or other disease onward to the ophthalmologist.

subject: PSM
q: Villagers in a Ganga-Brahmaputra delta region develop hyperkeratosis of the palms and soles along with patchy skin hyperpigmentation after years of drinking untreated tube-well water. Which environmental contaminant is responsible?
why: Fluoride causes dental/skeletal fluorosis (mottled enamel, genu valgum), not hyperkeratosis/hyperpigmentation
Lead causes neurotoxicity, anemia with basophilic stippling, and abdominal colic, not this skin picture
Cadmium is linked to itai-itai disease (bone/renal), not this presentation
Arsenicosis correctly matches both the geography and clinical picture
exp: Chronic arsenicosis from naturally contaminated groundwater (a well-documented problem in the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta belt of West Bengal/Bangladesh) causes characteristic hyperkeratosis, hyperpigmentation/hypopigmentation, and long-term skin cancer risk. Flag: confirm the current WHO/BIS permissible limit before quoting a number clinically.

subject: PSM
q: A new screening test has a sensitivity of 90% and a specificity of 80%. What is its positive likelihood ratio, and what does this value tell you about the test's usefulness?
why: This value would come from an incorrect formula/inversion
This is far too low to be the correct calculation and misreads the ratio
This is the correct calculation, falling in the small-to-moderate interpretation band
This is an inversion resembling a negative likelihood ratio, not LR+
exp: Positive likelihood ratio = sensitivity / (1 - specificity) = 0.9 / 0.2 = 4.5. By standard bands (>10 large, 5-10 moderate, 2-5 small, 1-2 minimal), an LR+ of 4.5 causes a small-to-moderate shift in post-test probability - clearly useful but not strongly confirmatory.

subject: PSM
q: A public health programme that shifts the blood pressure distribution of an entire population slightly downward (e.g. through salt-reduction policy) prevents more cardiovascular events overall than one that targets only individuals already at high risk, even though each individual's benefit is small. This principle is known as?
why: This correctly names Rose's population strategy paradox
The high-risk strategy targets only individuals above a risk threshold, the opposite approach described here
Herd immunity threshold is a vaccination-coverage concept, unrelated to this population risk-shift principle
Primordial prevention addresses upstream social determinants before risk factors emerge, a related but distinct concept
exp: Geoffrey Rose's prevention paradox states that a population-wide intervention offering small benefit to many individuals can prevent more disease overall than an intensive intervention offering large benefit to a few high-risk individuals, because most cases of common diseases arise from the much larger group at moderate risk.

subject: PSM
q: The Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) scheme delivers a package of six services to children under 6 years and pregnant/lactating women through Anganwadi Centres. Which of the following is NOT one of these six services?
why: One of the six ICDS services
One of the six ICDS services
Correct (the exception) - institutional delivery is not an ICDS service; it is delivered through the health system (JSY/PMSMA/facility-based care)
One of the six ICDS services
exp: ICDS's six services are Supplementary Nutrition, Immunization, Health Check-up, Referral Services, Pre-school Non-Formal Education, and Nutrition & Health Education - it is a nutrition/early-childhood-development platform delivered by the Anganwadi worker, not a facility that conducts institutional deliveries.

subject: PSM
q: As per Government of India Universal Immunization Programme guidance, a reconstituted BCG or Measles/MR vaccine vial must be discarded:
opts: Only at the end of the session, however long it runs
Within 4 hours of reconstitution, or at the end of the session, whichever is earlier
why: 28-day reuse applies to unopened liquid vaccines under the Open Vial Policy, not reconstituted freeze-dried vaccines
Not the standard cut-off used in Indian UIP guidance
Ignoring the 4-hour limit risks using a vaccine with degraded potency or contamination
Correct - 4 hours or end-of-session, whichever comes first
exp: Once a freeze-dried (lyophilised) vaccine like BCG or Measles/MR is reconstituted with diluent, it loses potency rapidly at room temperature and carries a contamination risk from repeated puncture - the Open Vial Policy's multi-session allowance applies only to unopened liquid vaccines, not reconstituted ones.

subject: PSM
q: As per the WHO simplified grading of goitre used in Iodine Deficiency Disorder (IDD) surveys, a goitre that is not visible but is palpable with the neck in a normal position is graded as:
why: Correct - palpable-not-visible defines Grade 1
Grade 0 means no palpable or visible goitre
Grade 2 means visible with the neck in normal position, a step beyond this description
There is no Grade 3 in the WHO simplified classification (older classifications had more grades, but the current WHO scheme is 0/1/2)
exp: WHO's simplified 3-point goitre grading (Grade 0 = no goitre; Grade 1 = palpable, not visible even with neck extended; Grade 2 = visible with neck in normal position) is the field-survey tool used to estimate community-level IDD burden and monitor salt-iodisation programmes.

subject: PSM
q: The declaration that established primary health care as the key strategy to achieve Health for All and identified it as the first level of contact between individuals and the health system was adopted at:
why: Ottawa Charter, 1986, is about health promotion strategies (build healthy public policy, create supportive environments), a later and different focus
Correct - Alma-Ata, 1978
Bangkok Charter, 2005, updated health promotion for a globalised world
Jakarta Declaration, 1997, was the 4th Global Conference on Health Promotion
exp: The 1978 Alma-Ata Declaration (International Conference on Primary Health Care, USSR) set the goal of Health for All by 2000 through primary health care as the cornerstone strategy - its principles (equity, community participation, intersectoral coordination, appropriate technology) still underpin India's PHC/HWC architecture.

subject: PSM
q: A 30-year-old farmer presents with high-grade fever, severe myalgia (especially calf muscles), conjunctival suffusion, and jaundice five days after wading through flood water contaminated with rodent urine. He now has oliguria and a rising creatinine. The most likely diagnosis is:
why: Scrub typhus classically has an eschar and is transmitted by chigger mite bite, not water exposure
DHF has thrombocytopenia, a rising haematocrit, and plasma leakage, but not the calf myalgia/conjunctival suffusion/jaundice triad
Correct - this vignette is textbook for leptospirosis
Enteric fever has stepladder fever and relative bradycardia, not conjunctival suffusion or this rapid renal decline pattern
exp: The combination of calf muscle tenderness, conjunctival suffusion, jaundice, and acute kidney injury after flood-water/rodent-urine exposure is the classic vignette for leptospirosis progressing to Weil's disease - a notifiable, occupationally-linked (farmers, sewage workers, sugarcane cutters) zoonosis that is common after flooding in India.

subject: PSM
q: A screening test for a disease with a population prevalence of 2 percent has a sensitivity of 90 percent and specificity of 95 percent. In a screened population of 10,000, approximately what proportion of those who test positive will actually have the disease (positive predictive value)?
why: 90 percent is the test's sensitivity, not its PPV in this population - a common distractor for students who confuse the two
95 percent is the specificity, not the PPV
approximately 53 percent is what you would get if you mistakenly used a much higher prevalence, a plausible arithmetic-error distractor
Correct - the calculated PPV at 2 percent prevalence
exp: With 200 truly diseased (2 percent of 10,000) and 9,800 truly non-diseased: true positives = 0.90 x 200 = 180; false positives = 0.05 x 9,800 = 490; PPV = 180 / (180+490) which is approximately 27 percent - this vignette demonstrates why even a good test performs poorly as a predictor in a low-prevalence population, the core reason mass screening programmes need a high-prevalence target group.

subject: PSM
q: After a stroke, a patient undergoes vocational retraining and has his home and workplace adapted to maximise residual function and enable a return to gainful employment despite persistent hemiparesis. As per Leavell and Clark's levels of prevention, this activity represents:
opts: Secondary prevention - early diagnosis and treatment
why: Correct - vocational retraining/return-to-work adaptation is the rehabilitation sub-stage of tertiary prevention
Secondary prevention happens during the subclinical-to-clinical window, before disability has set in, not after a completed stroke
Primary prevention (specific protection) acts before disease onset (e.g., BP control to prevent the stroke), not afterward

Disability limitation acts during the acute/active disease phase to limit the impairment itself (e.g., acute stroke unit care, early physiotherapy to limit contracture), a step earlier than vocational reintegration
exp: Leavell and Clark split tertiary prevention into two sequential sub-stages: disability limitation (preventing/minimising impairment while the disease process is still active) and rehabilitation (restoring the already-disabled individual to maximum functional and social usefulness afterward) - vocational retraining and environmental adaptation for return to work are the defining activities of the rehabilitation sub-stage specifically.

subject: PSM
q: Children in a village with groundwater fluoride levels of 6 ppm present with brown, mottled discolouration of tooth enamel and, in severe cases, genu valgum and spinal rigidity. This clinical picture is due to:
why: Iodine deficiency causes goitre and cretinism, not enamel mottling or skeletal rigidity
Correct - this is the classic endemic fluorosis vignette
Arsenicosis causes skin hyperpigmentation, hyperkeratosis, and skin cancers, not enamel/bone changes
Itai-itai (cadmium) disease causes osteomalacia and renal tubular damage, described originally in Japan, not this presentation
exp: Endemic fluorosis from high-fluoride groundwater (common in parts of Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu) produces mottled enamel at lower excess levels and, with prolonged high exposure, skeletal fluorosis (genu valgum/varum, spinal stiffness from ligament calcification) - it is a notified public-health problem addressed by safe water supply and defluoridation.

subject: PSM
q: Three infants who received pentavalent vaccine from the same vial at a rural immunization session develop high-grade fever and excessive crying within a few hours. As the Medical Officer, your most appropriate immediate action is to:
opts: Continue the ongoing session unchanged and simply monitor the children at home
Discard all other vaccine stocks in the entire facility cold chain as a precaution
Stop using vaccines from that specific vial/batch, manage the children clinically, and immediately report it as an AEFI cluster for investigation
Reassure the family and make no report, since fever after DPT-containing vaccines is universal
why: Ignoring a cluster risks missing a programmatic error and delays needed investigation and reporting
Discarding the entire cold chain stock is an overreaction not supported by evidence of a facility-wide problem
Correct - quarantine the implicated vial/batch, manage clinically, and report the AEFI cluster
Minor fever/crying is common after DPT-containing vaccines individually, but a temporally-clustered pattern from one vial still requires reporting and investigation, not dismissal
exp: A cluster of similar reactions from the same vial/batch is treated as a potential programmatic error or vaccine-quality issue until proven otherwise - the vial/batch is quarantined, cases are clinically managed and reported through the AEFI surveillance system, and a proper causality investigation (not blanket destruction of unrelated stock) follows.

subject: PSM
q: A 7-month-old, exclusively breastfed infant of a strict vegan mother (no vitamin supplementation during pregnancy or lactation) presents with pallor, poor feeding, and developmental regression. Peripheral smear shows macrocytosis with hypersegmented neutrophils. The most likely underlying deficiency is:
why: Iron deficiency causes microcytic, not macrocytic, anaemia
Folate deficiency can also cause megaloblastic change, but the classic vignette of a vegan-mother/breastfed-infant with neuro-regression is the B12 teaching point
Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets (bony changes), not macrocytic anaemia
Correct - maternal vegan diet without B12 supplementation is the classic cause of infantile B12 deficiency
exp: Exclusively breastfed infants of vegan or B12-deficient mothers are at risk of infantile vitamin B12 deficiency, which - unlike maternal B12 deficiency (often subclinical) - can present dramatically in the infant with irritability, developmental regression, failure to thrive, and megaloblastic anaemia with hypersegmented neutrophils, because the infant's B12 stores depend entirely on maternal status.

subject: PSM
q: At a Primary Health Centre, which cadre supervises the work of ANMs/Female Health Workers at the Sub-Centre level and additionally trains and monitors MCH service delivery?
why: The CHO clinically manages the upgraded Health and Wellness Centre but is not the traditional ANM-supervisory cadre.
The LHV is the designated supervisory and training cadre for ANMs/Female Health Workers, particularly for maternal and child health service quality.
An ASHA facilitator supports and mentors a cluster of ASHAs, not ANMs.
The Block Extension Educator handles health education/IEC activities at block level, not clinical supervision of ANMs.
